title: Read about event tracking
reading_goal: Understand event tracking, which records user behavior on a per-event basis.
question: What is the role of event tracking?
choices: To record user behavior on an event-by-event basis

title: Read the Privacy Opt-In
reading_goal: Understand "privacy opt-in," which involves obtaining user consent before collecting data for analysis.
question: What is the purpose of the privacy opt-in?
choices: To collect analytics data only when the user has given consent
answer: To collect analytics data only when the user has given consent
explanation: Privacy opt-in enables analytics only after the user makes an affirmative choice. Before consent, the app should neither create analytics events nor place them in a send queue. Explain what is collected and why, do not treat inaction as consent, and make withdrawal just as easy later.

title: Read about opting out
reading_goal: Understand the concept of "opt-out," which allows users to disable analytics data collection at any time.
question: Why is an opt-out option necessary?
choices: So users can stop analytics collection when they no longer want it
answer: So users can stop analytics collection when they no longer want it
explanation: Opt-out lets a user stop optional analytics collection. Changing a setting to false is only the start: event creation and transmission must stop immediately, and the app should explain how queued events and existing data are handled or deleted. Separating required feature data from optional analytics helps the core app keep working after withdrawal.

title: Read "Consent State"

question: What values can be assigned to the "consent" state?

The example's true value should be stored only after an affirmative action, never as a preselected default. If the user has not consented or has withdrawn, merely removing an identifier is not enough; the analytics events themselves must not be collected or sent.

answer: Because notes can contain a user's private learning records
explanation: Personal note text can contain private health, work, or account information, so it should not be sent in analytics events. title: Read anonymous ID
reading_goal: Understand the method of using anonymous IDs instead of personally identifiable information.
question: What is the purpose of an anonymous ID?
choices: To link usage events without using a direct identifier such as a name or email
answer: To link usage events without using a direct identifier such as a name or email
explanation: A random ID reduces the risk of using a name or email directly. Because it can still link repeated behavior, however, it is usually pseudonymous rather than truly anonymous, and combining it with other data may identify a person. Apply consent, access controls, rotation, and retention limits as well.

title: Read the privacy-safe metric
reading_goal: Understand how to assess quality using aggregated metrics without revealing individual data.
question: What is the key to the "privacy safe metric"?
choices: Evaluating app quality based on aggregated metrics rather than individual data
answer: Evaluating app quality based on aggregated metrics rather than individual data
explanation: Aggregating an average by level is less revealing than storing individual note text. Aggregation is not automatically safe, however: a group of one or two people or many combined filters may expose an individual. Use minimum group sizes, limited properties, retention rules, and access controls.

title: Reading the event queue
reading_goal: Understand the event queue, which temporarily stores events while offline and processes them later.
question: When is an event queue needed?
choices: To process events later when offline or when the network connection is unstable
answer: To process events later when offline or when the network connection is unstable
explanation: An event queue temporarily holds analytics events during an unstable connection. Surviving a reload may require a protected persistent store rather than an in-memory array, plus an expiration policy. Recheck current consent before sending; if the user withdrew, do not flush queued events and delete them according to policy.
